claim: American Airlines is opening its first Flagship Check-In at DFW in Terminal D near the D30 security checkpoint, with a separate entrance and dedicated processing for Flagship First / Flagship Business and eligible AAdvantage elites.
source_title: American unveils next-generation premium experience at DFW, featuring largest-ever Admirals Club lounge and enhanced Flagship services
supporting_excerpt: American's new Flagship check-in experience is located in Terminal D near the D30 security checkpoint and is scheduled to open later this year… Eligible travelers will have access to a separate entrance with personalized assistance and a more private check-in process before heading directly to security.
caveat: Announcement rather than opened facility; scope may shift before commissioning.

claim: American's Terminal F lounge posture at opening is a 'Provisions by Admirals Club' grab-and-go concept, not a Flagship-tier lounge, positioned as the first-phase lounge offering in Terminal F and expected to open with Terminal F Phase 1 in 2027.
source_title: American unveils next-generation premium experience at DFW, featuring largest-ever Admirals Club lounge and enhanced Flagship services
page_or_section: Body — Provisions by Admirals Club section
supporting_excerpt: A Provisions by Admirals Club lounge in DFW's future Terminal F will provide a grab-and-go experience in a streamlined, convenient setting… This space will serve as the first-phase lounge offering in Terminal F — and the first of American's suite of premium offerings planned for the new terminal.
caveat: American describes Provisions as the 'first' offering, leaving open the possibility of future tiers; the current announced scope for Terminal F remains grab-and-go.

claim: American's largest-ever Admirals Club, at approximately 37,000 square feet, is planned in Terminal C near the Skylink station — not in Terminal F.
source_title: American unveils next-generation premium experience at DFW, featuring largest-ever Admirals Club lounge and enhanced Flagship services
page_or_section: Body — Admirals Club Terminal C section
supporting_excerpt: A new Admirals Club opening in Terminal C, approximately 37,000 square feet, will be American's largest to date.
caveat: Announced; construction and opening dates as reported by American.

claim: DFW Terminal F is being built using a modular construction method with modules fabricated offsite and delivered by self-propelled modular transporter along an airside taxiway; six large module moves for Terminal F were completed by August 8 during a two-week nighttime window.
source_title: DFW Airport Completes Terminal F Module Moves As Sixth Terminal Takes Shape
supporting_excerpt: On Aug. 8, the airport completed the last of six module moves that make up the structure for Terminal F. The modules, some nearly as large as a football field, were moved overnight during a two-week period using self-propelled modular transporters along one of DFW's airside taxiways.
caveat: Descriptive of the initial structural modules only; downstream fit-out schedule not addressed.

claim: The Terminal F program was expanded from a 15-gate, approximately $1.6 billion scope to a 31-gate, approximately $4 billion scope, with American Airlines' Use and Lease Agreement extended through 2043; American is the sole occupant.
source_title: DFW Airport's Terminal F Rises With Record-Setting Modular Construction—and a Scaled-Up $4B Plan to Meet Global Demand
supporting_excerpt: The plan expanded from a $1.6 billion, 15-gate concept to an estimated $4 billion project featuring 31 gates… extending its lease at DFW through 2043.
caveat: Secondary source consolidating DFW and American announcements; exact figures should be reconciled with the U&L amendment text, which is not public in full.

claim: Research on airport signage using causal machine learning finds that high information density and text-only formats increase passenger cognitive load and reduce decision confidence, while text-plus-graphic formats improve wayfinding performance; time pressure moderates the effects.
source_title: Design mechanisms of airport visual guidance systems on passenger wayfinding performance: evidence from causal machine learning and a moderated mediation approach
supporting_excerpt: High information density and text-only formats increased cognitive load and reduced decision confidence, while text + graphic formats improved performance… time pressure as a moderator.
caveat: Findings are cross-sectional and moderated by time pressure; direct translation to a specific concourse requires local calibration.

claim: At Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport, approximately 80% of passenger information demand is satisfied when guidance information spacing is 47 meters, and 60% when spacing is 56 meters — providing an empirical bound on how far apart wayfinding signs can be before performance drops.
source_title: Design mechanisms of airport visual guidance systems on passenger wayfinding performance: evidence from causal machine learning and a moderated mediation approach
supporting_excerpt: At Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport, 80% of passenger information demand is satisfied when guidance information spacing is 47 m, and 60% of information demand is satisfied when the spacing is 56 m.
denominator: percent of passenger information demand satisfied
caveat: Single-airport case; corridor geometry and language differ from DFW; treat as directional benchmark.

claim: Charlotte Douglas consolidated five alpha-coded security zones into three numeric zones and reported that the change simplified passenger choices and reduced cognitive load; passengers there systematically overestimated walking-time distances, and the airport responded with real-time walk-time indicators, improved sightlines, and clarified decision points.
source_title: The Secret to Stress Free Airports? It Starts With Smart Design
page_or_section: Body — Charlotte Douglas / ACRP Report 52 section
supporting_excerpt: Research at Charlotte Douglas International Airport, drawing on 2,000 passenger surveys and extensive observation from ACRP Report 52, found that travelers consistently overestimated the time associated with walking distances… Consolidating five alpha coded security zones into three numeric ones simplified choices and reduced cognitive load.
caveat: Secondary summary of ACRP Report 52; primary report should be consulted for methodology detail.

claim: The Heathrow Terminal 5 opening in March 2008 resulted in over 42,000 bags misplaced in the first days after the baggage handling system was not fully tested and BA staff were not fully trained on the new system.
supporting_excerpt: BAA and BA only held joint meetings after things began to go wrong – namely issues with the baggage system, security searches and car parking – and the terminal's problems are considered to have been a direct result of this lack of co-operation, though poor staff training and system testing were also significantly contributory.
caveat: Contemporary retrospective; specific figures vary across accounts.

claim: American Airlines posted a 0.2% net margin in 2025 on $54.6 billion in revenue, compared with Delta's 7.9% and United's 5.7% net margins in the same period.
source_title: American's 2025 Earnings Look Awful Next To Delta And United
supporting_excerpt: American Airlines posted a 0.2% net margin in 2025, far below Delta's 7.9% and United's 5.7%. In 2025, American Airlines earned $54.6 billion in revenue but only $111 million in net income.
airport_or_entity: American Airlines / Delta Air Lines / United Airlines
units: percent net margin and USD revenue
caveat: Secondary source aggregating 10-K figures; primary carriers' 10-Ks are the audited record.

claim: American Airlines is targeting a 20% increase in premium seating by 2026 and 50% growth in premium capacity for widebody and long-haul aircraft by end of the decade, with the new Flagship Suite rolling out on 787-9, A321XLR, and 777-300ER retrofit aircraft.
source_title: Why American Airlines Is Doubling Down On Its Premium Product Across Its Widebody Fleet
supporting_excerpt: American Airlines is implementing a tiered growth strategy with a 20% increase in premium seating by 2026, with a long-term target of 50% growth in premium capacity for widebody and long-haul aircraft by the end of the decade. The company is targeting approximately 100 widebody aircraft for the new Flagship Suite.
units: percent premium seat growth and aircraft count
caveat: Trade-press summary of American's stated targets; program timelines are subject to fleet delivery slippage.

claim: A Multiple Aircraft Ramp System (MARS) gate is a gate configuration that can accommodate either one widebody aircraft or two narrowbody aircraft, and is used at busy hubs to preserve flexibility between widebody and narrowbody operations at the same physical position.
source_title: Airport Gates: Definitions, Allocation, and Financial Considerations
supporting_excerpt: A Multiple Aircraft Ramp System (MARS) gate is a flexible gate design that can accommodate either one widebody or two narrowbody aircraft at once. MARS gates use multiple lead-in lines, boarding bridges, and engineered clearances for different configurations.
caveat: Practitioner explainer; specific MARS geometries at DFW Terminal F are not publicly detailed.

claim: DFW's Capital Improvement Program totals approximately $11.3 billion through FY 2030, with Terminal F as one component alongside Terminal C and Terminal A renewals.
source_title: Airport Context Packet — DFW Terminal F, 2043 Horizon
supporting_excerpt: Capital Improvement Program: $11.3 billion through FY 2030 (per DWU Consulting summary of DFW disclosures). Terminal F is one component of a larger program that includes Terminal C and Terminal A renewals.
caveat: Context packet is a compiled summary of DFW disclosures via secondary aggregator; primary DFW CIP documents should confirm.

claim: American Airlines carried 82.6% of DFW's passengers in 2025 (70.8 million of 85.7 million) and operated 82% of departures; DFW-level connecting share is reported at approximately 60% while American's own hub materials describe DFW as its largest connecting complex.
source_title: Airport Context Packet — DFW Terminal F, 2043 Horizon
page_or_section: Section 4 — Airline use and lease context
supporting_excerpt: American Airlines carried 82.6% of DFW's passengers (70.8 million of 85.7 million) and operated 82% of departures (secondary sources citing DFW statistics)… DFW-level secondary reporting places connecting share at about 60%. American's own DFW hub materials describe DFW as the airline's largest connecting complex.
caveat: Airport-level vs carrier-level connecting share are not the same metric; the run prompt's two-thirds figure is at the carrier level.

claim: American Airlines' announced premium facilities at DFW comprise three distinct products: Flagship Check-In in Terminal D, a 37,000-square-foot Admirals Club in Terminal C, and a Provisions by Admirals Club grab-and-go in Terminal F — a tiered geographic placement where Terminal F is not the location of the top-tier products.
source_title: American Airlines Brings Flagship Check-In to DFW as It Chases Its Rivals
supporting_excerpt: The projects will give American three different premium facilities across DFW: a private pre-security check-in area, a conventional full-service lounge and a grab-and-go location.
caveat: Descriptive; American may add further Terminal F premium products in later phases.

claim: DFW's first-phase Terminal F is scheduled to open in 2027 with 15 gates as part of the expanded 31-gate program.
source_title: DFW Airport's Terminal F Rises With Record-Setting Modular Construction—and a Scaled-Up $4B Plan to Meet Global Demand
supporting_excerpt: The first phase of Terminal F is expected to open in 2027 with 15 gates.
caveat: Schedule as reported; subject to modular delivery and commissioning risk.
